function: DQN jointly controls UAV flight direction, UAV transmit power, IRS phase shifts and power-splitting ratio to maximize average GUE energy efficiency (pp. 2, 5-6).
system: Single-antenna UAV base station serves 15 ground users with SWIPT; one fixed passive reflecting IRS of 10-80 elements (UPA); Rician fading; band not stated (pp. 3, 8).
method: Deep Q-learning (DQN) with fully connected network, discrete actions, epsilon-greedy and experience replay; reward built from an SINR map with bivariate normal weighting; reinforcement learning (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: Own simulation: 300x300 m, 15 users, UAV at 100 m, IRS at 30 m; Rician factor 2, path-loss exponents 2.2 and 3.6; no standard channel model (pp. 3, 8).
test_conditions: One fixed GUE topology per trained model; the paper says any layout change needs retraining; sweeps over maximum power and IRS size (pp. 7-10).
baselines: SHF with random IRS phase (PS ratio 1, 0.5, <<1), a non-learned optimization scheme; DRL without IRS; REINFORCE; GS (gradient search with log-barrier, using DRL trajectory) (pp. 8-9).
metrics: Average energy efficiency (data rate over energy dissipation), average data rate, and GUE energy consumption versus maximum power and number of reflecting units (pp. 8-10).
complexity: Table I (p. 8): DRL complexity O(E I L N_act (N_con+2) N_IRS M^2), about 3.49e12 operations; REINFORCE 1e16, SHF 5.46e20, GS 1e10 operations.
q1_support: p. 3: "we utilize the channel model of Rician fading for both the UAV-GUE link and the IRS-GUE link." Not met: a custom Rician and LoS simulator (Table II, p. 8), with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 7: "any change in the GUE locations necessitates retraining the DRL model to reflect the new scenario accurately." Not met: the paper retrains for a new layout and tests no unseen condition; the sweeps of maximum power and IRS size (pp. 8-10) are not described as tests of a trained model.
q3_support: p. 8: "we select the SHF scheme [28] with random IRS phase steer, DRL without IRS, REINFORCE [29] and GS [30]." p. 9: "This figure shows that EE performance of the proposed algorithm is higher than that of the SHF."
q4_support: p. 8: "we can compute the computational complexity and the number of operation, which are summarized as in Table I", with the DRL complexity of eq. (31) and 3.49e12 operations in Table I.
q5_support: p. 8: "The Table II provides a summary of the parameters employed in the simulation." Not met: the channels are generated in the authors' simulation (p. 3), and no code or data link is given.
notes: Included as area 6 by the specificity order: the DQN controls the UAV transmit power and the IRS phase on an aerial link (pp. 5-6). The UAV route is above the physical layer but passes because it is learned jointly with physical-layer decisions. Area 3 is the alternative reading (IRS phase shifts); the reviewer should confirm. The system has single-antenna UAV and users but a RIS, so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply. q3 counts SHF with random IRS phase (non-learned) and REINFORCE (standard RL algorithm); DRL without IRS is a variant and does not count. Tables I-II (p. 8) and Figs. 7-12 (pp. 8-9) were read from page images.
